title: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies
abstract: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv. Math., 23(1) by Lieb and Simon. To demonstrate the potential and the limits of our method, we also compute explicit lower bounds for the ground-state energies $E(N,N)$ of all atoms with $2 \leq N \leq 86$ and we compare them with the bounds obtained in J. Chem. Phys., 62(8) by Hertel, Lieb, Thirring and the bounds obtained by Seco in his dissertation. Finally, we also provide a uniqueness result for the expectation values of the kinetic, potential and interaction energies on the ground-state space.
summary: This paper develops a novel, rigorous mathematical technique to compute lower bounds for the ground-state energies of atoms and ions. By establishing an improved explicit lower bound, it significantly advances the theoretical understanding of how electronic energy scales with nuclear charge and electron count. The methodology is purely analytical, providing deep mathematical tools for quantum many-body theory.
main_problem: The primary goal is establishing rigorous, mathematically derived lower bounds for the ground-state energies of atoms and ions, $E(N, Z)$. This is mathematically challenging because deriving lower bounds is significantly harder than finding upper bounds.
main_result: The authors establish a new iterative method yielding the explicit lower bound $E(N, Z) \geq -0.8710 N^{1/3}Z^2$, significantly improving previous estimates and approaching the Thomas-Fermi asymptotic limit.
method: The work employs a recursive, analytical method (Theorem 2.1) based on established mathematical inequalities and properties of the electronic Hamiltonian, avoiding purely numerical techniques.
model_or_system: The system is the electronic Hamiltonian for atoms/ions with $N$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z$, described by $H_N(Z)$. The analysis focuses on the ground-state energy $E(N, Z) = \inf \sigma(H_N(Z))$ and the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$.
key_observables: Ground-state energy $E(N, Z)$, the constant $A$ in the energy estimate, and the ionization capacity $N_c(Z)$.
important_parameters: Nuclear charge $Z$, number of electrons $N$, and the asymptotic limit $N 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the existence of a strictly monotonically increasing function $f(Z)$ that bounds $N_c(Z)$, and the analysis compares results against known Thomas-Fermi asymptotics.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, develops a recursive method (Theorem 2.1) for lower bounds, derives explicit bounds (Theorem 2.2), analyzes monotonicity properties (Theorem 2.4), and concludes with uniqueness results for expectation values.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical insights into the fundamental energy scaling laws of quantum many-body systems, which underpins the theoretical understanding of atomic structure relevant to AMO physics.
